definition: Buoyant means cheerful and resilient in spirit — able to stay light and rise back up after a blow, the way a float refuses to stay under.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word buoyant. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know buoyant should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Even after the moving van broke down twice, Dad stayed buoyant, turning the second roadside wait into a picnic.
Hopeful is weaker than buoyant: a hopeful mood looks for better days but can still sink, while buoyant spirits actually rise back every time something pushes them down.
Irrepressible goes further than buoyant: buoyant spirits dip and then recover, but irrepressible ones cannot be held down even for a moment.

Lighthearted means carefree and cheerful in the moment — a lighthearted joke or afternoon carries no weight at all. Buoyant adds the rebound: buoyant spirits have felt the weight and keep rising back anyway, the way a float pops up after every wave.

Optimistic means expecting things to turn out well — it is a judgment about the future. Buoyant describes the felt lift of the mood itself: you hear optimism in a forecast, but you see buoyancy in someone knocked flat at noon and humming again by two.

Halfway through the 400-mile charity ride, Tess's derailleur snapped, a headwind rose, and the rain started.
She coasted into the rest stop grinning anyway, borrowed a wrench from a stranger, and by nightfall was leading the camp singalong.
"You can't sink her," her teammate laughed — and it was true: every setback pushed Tess's mood under for a minute, and every time it bobbed right back up, buoyant as a cork.
Tess's spirits are not merely cheerful — they are repeatedly pushed down and keep surfacing.
That refusal to stay sunk, the mood that rises back after every blow, is exactly what buoyant describes.

Buoyant praises a mood for its bounce, not its volume.

Keep it apart from this unit's other bright words: vivacious is outward social sparkle that fills a room, and euphoric is a soaring high — buoyant is quieter and tougher, spirits that take a hit and rise anyway.
It also differs from optimistic, which is a judgment that things will go well; buoyancy is the lift you can watch in someone's manner, whatever they predict.

Marisol's food truck had a cursed first summer.
The generator died during her very first lunch rush, a June hailstorm dented the new awning, and the county moved her permitted corner twice in one month.
Her crew braced for gloom after every piece of bad news, and every time the gloom never quite arrived.
Marisol would go quiet for an hour, then reappear buoyant, sketching a new menu on the whiteboard and teasing the cooks about the weather.
By August the crew had stopped worrying about bad news at all; whatever landed, the mood in the truck always seemed to rise back before the dinner shift.
